{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Parse revenue: remove commas and convert to float
df['revenue'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# The question asks for conversion rate in the sales data — all rows
# 'converted' = 1 if the order completed checkout, per data dictionary
# This is independent of 'status' — so we use all rows, not just 'completed'
# Conversion rate = number of converted orders / total number of orders (all rows)

# Compute conversion rate by customer_segment over all orders
cross_tab = pd.crosstab(df['customer_segment'], df['converted'], margins=True)

# Extract conversion rate for each segment
converted_count = cross_tab[1]  # number of converted orders per segment
total_orders = cross_tab['All']  # total orders per segment
conversion_rates = converted_count / total_orders

# Find the segment with highest conversion rate
best_segment = conversion_rates.idxmax()

# Print conversion rates for all segments
total_orders = cross_tab['All']
converted = cross_tab[1]
conversion_rates = converted / total_orders

print("Conversion rates by segment (all orders, including refunded):")
for seg, rate in conversion_rates.items():
    print(f"  {seg}: {rate:.4f} ({converted[seg]} / {total_orders[seg]})")

# Output the best segment
print(f"\nHighest conversion rate: {best_segment}")"}
